sourceInformation.source: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (1984), David Crane / Activision
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL2 fallback, TSL cel lighting; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded 3D diorama with ink outlines, faceted stone, jade foliage, amber ruins and turquoise water
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer with original idle, run, jump, fall, climb, swim and balloon clips; procedural creatures and scenery
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized adaptive adventure music, effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 cooperative players; AI Hub host-authoritative shared world; standalone same-browser BroadcastChannel and direct WebRTC invitation/reply; no relay supplied
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless testing allowed; one quiet command; screenshots for visual review only; no FPS target. Chromium153 WebGPU/SwiftShader and WebGL2; complete scripted route with invulnerability, separate hazards, keyboard, virtual standard gamepad, emulated touch, same-file and two-page co-op, real WebRTC, offline audio analysis, official Hub latency/loss/host-leave/playerless-server harness. Physical controller, real mobile hardware and human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: 1984 Atari 2600 manual via AtariAge; AtariAge screenshots; AtariOnline soundtrack/gameplay overview; official AI Hub protocol, session client and harness; Rapier character-controller documentation

testingFeedback: 122/122 final checks passed. 15 game issues caught and fixed: 3 by automated runs and 12 during review. Test-script mistakes are excluded.
2 progression-breaking issues: blocked riverbank ladder descent and co-op replay not resuming the guest. Both fixed.

The full scripted cavern route, which caught the blocked descent and verifies every movement mode, all three objectives and the ending. Multiplayer restart and native file-launch checks cover the packaged release.
Syntax-only checks; they cannot verify physics, controls, graphics or progression.
engineFeedback: Three.js native animation clips and TSL made it possible to combine a layered 3D illustration with stepped cel lighting.
An unsupported flatShading property on MeshBasicNodeMaterial emitted warnings; removed it and retained the geometry normals and quantized lighting.
The movement state machine, expedition progression, controller menus, cooperative authority and procedural audio.
Combining ladder, swimming and balloon movement with Rapier character-controller queries for two independent explorers.
Provide a WebGPU-ready toon material and a small input/character-controller framework in the standard examples.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source, controller-first philosophy, single-file deliverable and explicit testing requirements.
No plan file was supplied, so plan is none. Cross-device multiplayer specifies no lobby or relay service.
Delivering all movement modes, co-op authority, attract play, controller menus and procedural art/audio as one portable file.
Specify a multiplayer lobby/relay, or explicitly accept manual direct-peer invitations and their network limitations.

aiHub.name: Pit & Away: Lost Caverns
aiHub.description: Descend through inked ruins, swim a glowing archive and ride a balloon to the Sunstone Vault. Rescue two wayward friends in a forgiving solo or two-player cavern expedition.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD/arrows: move, climb and swim; Cross/A/Space: jump or release balloon; Triangle/Y/M: map; Options/Escape: pause; touch: left drag and contextual right action.
